item.title: 🗓 On October 31, the meeting of the #G20 Foreign Ministers under the US chairmanship concluded in Atlanta, Georgia, USA
item.description: 🗓 On October 31, the meeting of the #G20 Foreign Ministers under the US chairmanship concluded in Atlanta, Georgia, USA . On October 31,
the meeting
of the
#G20
Foreign Ministers under the US chairmanship concluded in Atlanta, Georgia, USA

Sergey Lavrov
.
🎙
Sergey Lavrov's presser following the G20 Ministerial
During the meeting, the Parties held
a substantive discussion on a wide range of current international issues
, focusing on the interplay between economic challenges and geopolitical instability.
Sergey Lavrov outlined Russia’s views on the factors fuelling global tensions
, with particular emphasis on energy and food security and the smooth operation of supply chains and shipping routes on an open, non-discriminatory basis.
He stressed the importance of
strengthening
a
#MultipolarWorld
order,
reforming
global economic governance, and
countering
unfair competition and neo-colonial practices.
The participants offered
detailed assessments of destructive actions that undermine international trade
, including the interception of merchant vessels, sanctions, asset seizures and other unscrupulous methods.
☝️
Russia reaffirmed its commitment to remaining
a reliable trading partner
and
a leading supplier of energy, food and fertilisers to countries in need
.
The discussion also highlighted
Russia’s considerable transport and logistics potentia
l, including opportunities to expand the capacity of
the Northern Sea Route
.
👉
The parties underscored the unifying nature of
President Vladimir Putin’s initiative to establish a Greater Eurasian Partnership
and of efforts to build
a common security architecture in Eurasia
.
***
As is customary, Sergey Lavrov held a series of contacts on the sidelines of the event with his counterparts, including US Secretary of State
Marco Rubio
, India’s External Affairs Minister
Subrahmanyam Jaishankar
, Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister
Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud
, Indonesia’s Foreign Minister
Arrmanatha Nasir
and Japan’s Foreign Minister
Toshimitsu Motegi
, among others.

item.title: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s statement on the expiry of the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara
item.description: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s statement on the expiry of the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (November 1, 2026) 💬 On October 31, the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara expired . Although consensus on a final settlement of the Western Sahara issue has yet to be reached, the US, seeking to artificially accelerate the settlement process, began insisting on the eve of that date on a drastic reduction in the Mission's powers , including abandoning the organisation of a referendum, even though the directly interested parties, including Morocco and Algeria, agreed on the importance of giving the people of Western Sahara the opportunity to determine their own destiny. ❌ Russia could not support the intention to deprive the people of Western Sahara of their right to vote , but the US opposed extending the previous mandate, thereby bringing the Mission to the brink of liquidation . We regret the removal of the basis for the presence of UN representatives in Western Sahara. Nevertheless, we expect the political settlement process to continue, making it possible to find, among the various options for the territory’s status, the solution best suited to the local population . We remain in close contact with our Algerian, Moroccan and other partners on this issue.

item.title: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s answer to a media question
item.description: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s answer to a media question on the current situation surrounding Iran (November 2, 2026) ❓ Question: Recent media reports suggest that new military action against Iran is being planned. How would you comment on the current situation surrounding Iran? 💬 Maria Zakharova: The situation surrounding Iran, which has been subjected to unprovoked aggression by the US and Israel , remains complex . The conflict is still unresolved and continues to reverberate across the Middle Eas t, intertwining with other crises in the region. Reports that further military action against the Islamic Republic is being planned are a cause for grave concern . The tragic experience of recent months demonstrates that military ventures sowing death and destruction in Iran cannot break the Iranian people’s resolve to defend their country’s sovereignty and independence . 👉 Those threatening new strikes today should reflect on this . We believe diplomatic efforts to normalise the situation must be stepped up. We support the mediators’ efforts and are helping to advance the negotiating process. ❗️ We reaffirm our readiness to contribute both to finding mutually acceptable solutions and to their subsequent implementation . Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov discussed these issues with Arab and Iranian representatives during his recent visit to the region . 🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s
answer to a media question
on the current situation surrounding Iran
(November 2, 2026)
❓
Question: Recent media reports suggest that new military action against Iran is being planned. How would you comment on the current situation surrounding Iran?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
The situation surrounding Iran, which has been subjected to
unprovoked aggression by the US and Israel
, remains
complex
.
The conflict is still unresolved and continues to reverberate across the Middle Eas
t, intertwining with other crises in the region.
Reports that further military action against the Islamic Republic is being planned are
a cause for grave concern
.
The tragic experience of recent months demonstrates that military ventures sowing death and destruction in Iran
cannot break the Iranian people’s resolve to defend their country’s sovereignty and independence
.
👉
Those threatening new strikes today
should reflect on this
.
We believe diplomatic efforts to normalise the situation must be stepped up.
We support the mediators’ efforts and are helping to advance the negotiating process.
❗️
We reaffirm our readiness to contribute both to finding mutually acceptable solutions and to their subsequent implementation
. Russia's Foreign Minister
Sergey Lavrov
discussed these issues with Arab and Iranian representatives during
his recent visit to the region
.
We hope that the situation in the Strait of Hormuz will return to normal as soon as possible
, with due regard for the legitimate interests of both the littoral states and countries seeking safe and unimpeded passage through this waterway, which is vital to the global economy. This applies fully to Iran as well, as it faces an unlawful US naval blockade.
We welcome the high-level meeting
held in Tehran on October 26 between Iran and the parties to
the so-called Mecca Pact
. Constructive dialogue between neighbours, the restoration of mutual trust and mutual respect for security interests are
essential
.
☝️
This approach underpins
Russia’s Concept of Collective Security in the Persian Gulf,
which seeks to promote
an indivisible security architecture in this strategically important region
, free from destructive outside interference.

⚡️
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's
statement
on the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists
(
November 2, 2026)
💬
November 2 marks
the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists
,
established in 2013
by a
#UN
General Assembly resolution.
This observance aims to draw global attention to
the need to protect journalists as they carry out their professional duties
and to reinforce the principle that
atrocities committed against them must inevitably be punished
.
❗️
We have to acknowledge that the actual situation regarding journalists’ safety has not improved and
continues to steadily deteriorate.
Over these years,
the media landscape has turned into a full-fledged theatre of war
, where the countries of the “collective West”, clinging to their former hegemony, use every means available to suppress dissent and impose on the
#GlobalMajority
the “only correct” view of world events.
Repressive actions by the West and its protégés
in
Ukraine
,
Moldova
and t
he Baltic states
against Russian media outlets and their staff have still not received an adequate response from the relevant international organisations –
the UN Human Rights Office
,
UNESCO
,
the OSCE
and others.
Emboldened by unchecked impunity, the Kiev regime is openly conducting a relentless hunt for members of the Russian media community.
War correspondents on the front line know better than anyone that
the blue “PRESS” patch
on a bulletproof vest, which once offered protection against targeted fire, has become
a convenient target for Ukrainian Banderites
– visible from afar and used to direct deliberate attacks.
Such attacks constitute
war crimes
under
international humanitarian law
, yet the relevant international bodies fail to direct criticism at those responsible.
🕯
In the 13 years since
the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists
was established,
dozens of talented professionals have been killed by Ukrainian militants
, including:
▪️
Igor Kornelyuk
▪️
Anton Voloshin
▪️
Andrey Stenin
▪️
Anatoly Klyan
▪️
Daria Dugina
▪️
Oleg Klokov
▪️
Maxim Fomin
(Vladlen Tatarsky)
▪️
Rostislav Zhuravlev
▪️
Boris Maksudov
▪️
Semyon Yeryomin
▪️
Valery Kozhin
▪️
Nikita Tsisagi
▪️
Yulia Kuznetsova
▪️
Alexander Martemyanov
▪️
Alexander Fedorchak
▪️
Andrey Panov
▪️
Anna Prokofyeva
▪️
Nikita Goldin
▪️
Ivan Zuev
***
👉
Another regrettable consequence of the toxic politicisation of journalists’ protection is that many of the Russian correspondents named above were
once again omitted
from the newly published
UNESCO Director-General’s Report on the Safety of Journalists for 2024-2025
.
Although, at our insistence, a link to official Russian data on all such crimes was finally included in an annex to the report
, the document itself continues to take a selective approach to statistics.
We consider it necessary to recall that
the 1997 General Conference resolution
and
the 2023 Executive Board decision
require UNESCO’s leadership
to condemn the killing of journalists and acts of physical violence
against them without distinction.
#NoStatuteOfLimitations
There is NO statute of limitations for crimes against Russian journalists
.
☝️
Russia will not back down from its legitimate demands within UNESCO and other relevant frameworks
.
The Russian MFA
will continue to consistently defend the professional rights of Russian journalists abroad, work to create safe conditions for their activities and seek just punishment for those responsible for crimes against them.
